As part of efforts to increase access to vehicle ownership in the country, Sterling Bank Limited has partnered with Nigerian Sinotrucks Limited to advance integrated mobility and financial solutions. According to a release signed by the Public Relations Lead, Sterling Bank Ltd, Olufisayo Osindeinde, and obtained by The PUNCH on Wednesday, the collaboration is expected to open new opportunities for individuals, entrepreneurs and businesses that depend on commercial vehicles to grow. It noted that the agreement, formalised through the signing of a Memorandum of Agreement at Sterling Towers in Lagos, targeted one of the major constraints in the mobility market: access to appropriate financing for vehicle acquisition. Speaking at the signing, Divisional Head, Commercial Banking at Sterling Bank, Akporee Idenedo, said the partnership reflected the bank’s conviction that financial institutions and mobility providers have to work together to unlock growth. “Transportation is the backbone of commerce. Every truck on the road is a supply chain moving, a business expanding, jobs being created and sustained. Yet for many entrepreneurs and businesses, the cost of acquiring the right vehicle remains a major barrier. Through this partnership with Nigerian Sinotrucks, we are bringing financing directly to the point of need, so customers can access quality vehicles on terms that are practical and fit their realities. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources “At Sterling Bank, we believe the most meaningful financial solutions are the ones that solve real problems. This collaboration lets us support individuals and businesses who want to own their vehicles, while helping to build a more efficient and productive transportation ecosystem for the country,” he asserted. He noted that the partnership sits squarely within transportation, one of the five pillars of Sterling Bank’s HEART strategy, alongside Health, Education, Agriculture and Renewable Energy. Osindeinde added that anchored on the theme “From Partnership to Progress: Advancing Integrated Mobility and Financial Solutions”, the partnership paired the lender’s financial capabilities with Nigerian Sinotrucks’ commercial vehicle expertise, countrywide maintenance infrastructure, driver training centres and market presence to create a more accessible and efficient vehicle ownership proposition. Sinotrucks, Sterling Bank partner to boost vehicle ownership COP31: Delegates stranded as transport delays hit Türkiye Stallion Group Partners With Access Bank “By bringing financing more directly into the vehicle acquisition process, the partnership is designed to ease the capital constraints that often prevent individuals and businesses from investing in the vehicles they need, and to support customers across logistics, manufacturing, distribution, construction and other transport-dependent sectors,” he explained. According to the Managing Director of Nigerian Sinotrucks, Alfred Okugbeni, the agreement is another step in its ambition to deepen its footprint in Nigeria’s automotive and transportation ecosystem. He highlighted that the collaboration was driven by the company’s determination to go beyond vehicle supply and respond to the broader needs of customers. “At Nigerian Sinotrucks, we understand that access to reliable vehicles is only one part of the mobility equation. Access to appropriate financing is equally important. Our partnership with Sterling Bank is a deliberate effort to bridge that gap and create greater opportunities for individuals and businesses to acquire the vehicles they need to grow. “We believe that when mobility and finance work together, the benefits extend beyond vehicle ownership. They translate into stronger businesses, improved logistics, greater productivity and wider economic opportunities,” he said. Nigerian Sinotrucks’ portfolio spans heavy-duty commercial vehicles, including HOWO tractor heads, dump trucks, tippers, cargo trucks, tankers and other specialised vehicles. The company has also expanded its alternative-energy offerings with CNG- and LNG-powered trucks, and recently introduced Sitrak electric commercial trucks into the Nigerian market. Felix Oloyede
